items.title: BI 250 Nima Dehghani: How Brains Compute
items.summary: Support the show to get full episodes, full archive, and join the Discord community.The Transmitter is an online publication that aims to deliver useful information, insights and tools to build bridges across neuroscience and advance research. Visit thetransmitter.org to explore the latest neuroscience news and perspectives, written by journalists and scientists.Read more about our partnership.Sign up for Brain Inspired email alerts to be notified every time a new Brain Inspired episode is released.To explore more neuroscience news and perspectives, visit thetransmitter.org.Nima Dehghani is a computational and theoretical neuroscientist at MIT. His work is framed by what he calls an N4 framework: neurophysics, neurocomputation, neurodynamics, and, encompassing them all, neuro-AI. We have a wide ranging discussion, mostly revolving around his work and views on how brains - and physical systems in general - perform computations to carry out their functions. Most neuroscientists more or less casually use the term computation to describe whatever it is the brain might be doing, but Nima is focused on a principled account of how the various parts of our brains work, how they compose together, and what those compositions can achieve across the many scales of the brain and within the massive recurrence of the brain.
